key_insight: SpeakerMem-R1 introduces a speaker-centered memory framework for multi-party dialogue, aiming to preserve who said what, who relates to whom, and how group knowledge evolves over time. It tackles the fact that standard long-term memory systems often blur person-level and group-level relationships.
problem_solved: The paper addresses long-term memory retrieval in multi-party conversations, where useful information is distributed across speakers, references, and time. The core challenge is maintaining accurate speaker attribution, interpersonal relations, shared group knowledge, and temporal state changes.
method: Uses a dual-track memory design centered on speakers and dialogue context.
Separates and tracks person-specific, relation-specific, and group-shared information over time.
Integrates dispersed clues from long conversations to support more accurate memory retrieval and reasoning.
impact: This matters because real-world conversational AI must handle complex group interactions, not just isolated Q&A. Better speaker-aware memory can improve assistants, meeting summarizers, social chatbots, and any system that needs reliable multi-party understanding.
visual_elements: A two-track memory pipeline diagram showing speaker-centered and group-centered memory streams.
A multi-party dialogue timeline with colored speaker labels and evolving relationship links.
An information map illustrating who said what, who knows what, and what is shared by the group.
An error comparison chart showing reduced confusion between speakers and relations versus baseline memory systems.
paper_title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
paper_authors: Haobo Zheng, Tan Tang, Yan Chen, Weijie Wang, Yingcai Wu
